findings.title: Missing @payable Decorator Prevents Contract Compilation
findings.description: The deposit() function accesses msg.value but does not include the @payable decorator. In Vyper 0.3.9, external functions default to nonpayable. Accessing msg.value from a nonpayable function raises NonPayableViolation, preventing compilation and deployment of this contract.

findings.title: Limited Gas Stipend Can Prevent Smart Contract Wallet Withdrawals
findings.description: Vyper's send() operation forwards the EVM's 2300 gas stipend for nonzero ETH transfers when no additional gas is specified. If a user deposits through a smart contract wallet whose receiving function requires more than 2300 gas, withdraw() will revert. This can prevent that wallet from accessing its deposited funds through this withdrawal function. This is an availability and compatibility issue, not a reentrancy vulnerability.
findings.recommendation:
Consider replacing send() with raw_call() using an appropriately selected gas limit and revert_on_failure=True. Preserve the existing nonreentrancy protection and Checks-Effects-Interactions ordering. Test withdrawals using both EOAs and smart contract wallets.

Reference: https://docs.vyperlang.org/en/v0.3.9/built-in-functions.html

summary: The contract has a sound basic withdrawal design, but it cannot compile as written because deposit() is missing @payable. After correcting this issue, the state-changing functions share the same @nonreentrant("withdraw") lock, which protects against reentrant calls between deposit() and withdraw(). The withdrawal function also follows the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern by updating the user's balance before sending ETH. Vyper's built-in uint256 arithmetic protection prevents ordinary integer overflow and underflow. getBalance() is read-only and cannot modify contract state. The remaining identified concern is the 2300-gas stipend limitation of send(), which may prevent some smart contract wallets from withdrawing. No direct fund-draining vulnerability or exploitable reentrancy vulnerability was identified in the provided logic.
